summary.text: 坐 represents sitting or remaining in place. One explanation pictures people sitting on the ground; another reads a Warring States form as a kneeling figure over ground, with a later alteration to its upper part.

formation.text: The character is best treated as semantic: its proposed constructions convey posture and ground, with no documented phonetic component. The two-people-on-ground account differs from an analysis of Warring States forms as 卩 over 土, a kneeling person on the ground. That analysis reports Qin forms with doubled 卩 and proposes that alteration of the upper form led Shuowen to read it as shortened 畱. This sequence is a proposed graphic history; the Shang identification as 坐 is tentative. Shuowen’s account records a Han-period interpretation, not independent confirmation of the earlier structure.

components.text: In the reported Warring States analysis, 卩 depicts a kneeling person within an earlier form of 坐. Qin forms are described as using doubled 卩, followed by alteration; 卩 is not claimed as a component of the modern graph.
土 depicts the ground in the Warring States kneeling-person analysis; the two-people account also identifies the ground as 土. Its presence in modern 坐 does not by itself settle the competing accounts.

Shuowen read the upper form as shortened 畱 and connected it with stopping or remaining. A competing analysis traces the Qin upper form to altered doubled 卩; 畱 is therefore Shuowen’s interpretation, not an established earlier component.

history.text: A seal-style rendering illustrates the received form associated with Shuowen’s analysis of 土 and shortened 畱. It is a modern reconstruction, not a dated artifact or proof of the graph’s earlier structure.
Historical variants are recorded, and standard 坐 is described as the regular-script form of the ancient graph. The variants do not establish one direct line of development.
A proposed relationship between 坐 and 危 remains unsettled; it is not established here as a graphic ancestor or component relationship.

uncertainties.text: The two-people-on-ground explanation and the 卩-over-土 analysis are competing accounts. The latter’s proposed Qin alteration path is reported as an analysis, not a sequence directly verified from primary glyphs.
The Shang identification as 坐 is tentative. Cited classical examples do not establish securely dated manuscript witnesses or a firm chronology among the senses.
No phonetic component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed in the cited analyses; readings of 坐 alone do not establish a sound role for any part.

senses.gloss: sit; remain in a seated or kneeling posture
senses.text: Classical textual examples are reported for sitting or kneeling, but the surviving witnesses are not dated here, and this use is not thereby established as the character’s original meaning.
Cited texts show 坐 used for a seat or place; they do not date this use relative to the sitting sense.
Cited examples record uses meaning stay or keep watch, without establishing when they arose or whether they developed from sitting.

senses.gloss: be implicated or convicted; legal confrontation
senses.text: Classical examples are cited for these legal uses, but their chronology and relationship to the sitting sense are unresolved.
A causal use is reported in poetic texts; its development from another sense or by another process is not established.

senses.gloss: ride or travel by a vehicle
senses.text: 坐 is also used for riding or traveling by vehicle, but the cited examples do not establish how this use developed.

developments.text: Both uses are attested, but the evidence does not establish that the seat or place sense developed from sitting.
The cited uses do not establish a semantic transition from sitting to staying or keeping watch.
No semantic path from sitting to the legal uses is demonstrated.
The causal use is attested, but its derivation from sitting is not established.
The dictionary gloss for riding or travel by vehicle does not establish a semantic development from sitting.

limitations.text: Shuowen and Duan Yucai give a semantic account involving stopping or remaining, sitting on a mat, and placing or resting something. It does not date each proposed extension or establish a path to all later uses.
Cited dictionary examples document several uses but do not establish their chronology or a complete set of semantic relationships.

overview.text: 坐 means ‘sit’ or ‘remain seated.’ One account pictures people on the ground; another reads an earlier form as a kneeling person over ground, with its upper part later altered.

components.text: In one earlier-form analysis, 卩 pictures a kneeling person; it is not treated as a separate part of modern 坐.
土 is the ground in both the kneeling-person analysis and the account of people sitting on the ground.
Shuowen read the upper part as shortened 畱; another analysis traces it to altered doubled 卩.

takeaway.text: The accounts share the idea of sitting or remaining, but they do not establish one shared analysis of the ancient graph.

relationships.text: In the reported Warring States analysis, 卩 depicts a kneeling person in an earlier form of 坐. The analysis reports later alteration, so this is not asserted as a current component.
土 depicts the ground in the Warring States kneeling-person analysis; the separate two-people account also identifies ground as 土.

Shuowen interpreted the upper form as shortened 畱 and linked it with stopping or remaining. A competing analysis traces that area to altered doubled 卩, so 畱 is not asserted as the earlier graphic identity.
